summary: This lecture begins the story of the Isra' and Mi'raj, the most widely narrated event and the hardest to arrange chronologically. The ustaz explains that Isra' is the journey on earth and Mi'raj the journey to the heavens, states the ruling on rejecting them, gives three contexts to understand (the sirah, Bayt al-Maqdis and the Roman-Persian world), and lists six opinions on its timing before choosing the view that it came after the deaths of Khadijah RA and Abu Talib and after Ta'if. He then covers the opening of the chest with wisdom and faith, the Buraq, three prayer stops, the prophets gathering and being led by the Prophet ﷺ, the choice of milk over wine, and the meetings in the first to seventh heavens with Adam, Isa and Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa and Ibrahim. He closes with the wisdom of the journey: strengthening the Prophet ﷺ in his grief, the gift of the prayer that is our own mi'raj, and Masjid al-Aqsa as a place that must not be removed from the ummah's memory.
keyPoints: Isra' is the journey on earth to Masjid al-Aqsa and Mi'raj the journey to the heavens, and both must be believed in.
It came when the Prophet ﷺ was at his lowest point after losing Khadijah RA, Abu Talib and the events of Ta'if.
The Prophet's ﷺ heart was filled with wisdom and faith before the journey, and he met the prophets and led them in prayer.
The Prophet ﷺ chose milk, not wine, and Jibril said it was a good choice.
Allah showed the Prophet ﷺ that when every door on earth is shut, the door of heaven is always open.
Prayer is the gift from the heavens, and the greatest crisis is when our relationship with Allah is cut off.

chapters.title: Opening and Prophet Ibrahim AS
chapters.summary: The ustaz returns to Makkah after Dhul-Hijjah and presents the whole sirah as the answer to Prophet Ibrahim's prayer.

chapters.title: The most complex story and two events
chapters.summary: The Isra' and Mi'raj is narrated by more than 20 Companions, and the ustaz distinguishes Isra' from Mi'raj and the ruling on denying them.

chapters.title: Three contexts of the event
chapters.summary: The textual context, the life of the Prophet, the context of Bayt al-Maqdis and the world context: the clash of Rome and Persia.

chapters.title: When did it happen?
chapters.summary: Six opinions on the timing, and the choice of Safiur Rahman al-Mubarakfuri that it came after Khadijah RA's death and before the Hijrah.

chapters.title: The lowest point in the Prophet's ﷺ life
chapters.summary: The deaths of Khadijah RA and Abu Talib and the Ta'if episode, and the return to Makkah under the protection of Mut'im ibn Adi.

chapters.title: Two gifts before the trial: Qur'an and night prayer
chapters.summary: Allah gave revelation and night prayer before the great trial, and the Prophet had no ally in Makkah.

chapters.title: Ummu Hani's house and the opening of the chest
chapters.summary: Two versions of how it began: in Ummu Hani's house or at Hijr Isma'il, and the Prophet's chest was opened and washed with zamzam.

chapters.title: Wisdom and faith, and the many versions
chapters.summary: Wisdom and faith were placed in the Prophet's chest as preparation, and the ustaz explains why the narrations are hard to arrange.

chapters.title: The Buraq, vehicle of the prophets
chapters.summary: The Buraq is white, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, and the Prophet rode it after Jibril rebuked it.

chapters.title: The first verse of Surah al-Isra'
chapters.summary: Allah begins with Subhanallah, and the ustaz explains the journey was in body and soul, which is what makes it miraculous.

chapters.title: Three prayer stops
chapters.summary: The Prophet stopped at Taibah (Madinah), at the tree of Prophet Musa in Madyan or Sinai, and at Bayt Lahm where Prophet Isa was born.

chapters.title: The prophets gather and are led in prayer
chapters.summary: At Bayt al-Maqdis the Prophet saw Musa and Isa, tied the Buraq and led the prophets in congregational prayer.

chapters.title: Three mosques and the choice of milk or wine
chapters.summary: The three mosques one may travel to, the building of Masjid al-Haram and al-Aqsa, and the Prophet's choice of milk.

chapters.title: First heaven: Adam AS and two rivers
chapters.summary: The gates of heaven are guarded by angels who ask questions, the Prophet met Adam AS with his offspring, and saw the Nile and Euphrates.

chapters.title: The second to seventh heavens
chapters.summary: Meetings with Isa and Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa who wept, and Ibrahim leaning on the Bayt al-Ma'mur.

chapters.title: Wisdom of the journey and closing
chapters.summary: Strengthening the Prophet's faith, the gift of prayer, the prophets united at al-Aqsa, the Prophet's mercy growing, and prayer as our mi'raj.

dalil.context: The ustaz presents the whole sirah as the answer to Prophet Ibrahim's prayer.
dalil.translation: I am the answer to the prayer of my father Ibrahim.

dalil.context: Surah ar-Rum says the Romans were defeated and Allah foretold their victory, which coincided with the victory at Badr. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: The Byzantines have been defeated

dalil.context: One reason the ustaz chooses the view that the Isra' and Mi'raj came after Khadijah RA's death.
dalil.translation: Khadijah RA died before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.

dalil.context: Night prayer was one of the two great gifts from Allah to the Prophet before the trial. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Stay up throughout the night, all but a small part of it,

dalil.context: Half the night, or a little less, as the Prophet's spiritual routine. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: half, or a little less,

dalil.context: The command to recite the Qur'an slowly in the night prayer. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: or a little more; recite the Quran slowly and distinctly:

dalil.context: The ustaz notes one version uses the words knowledge and certainty, graded hasan.
dalil.translation: Jibril opened the Prophet's chest, washed it with zamzam water, then poured wisdom and faith from a golden vessel into his chest and closed it again.

dalil.context: Buraq comes from 'barq', meaning lightning, and the hadith describes it.
dalil.translation: The Buraq was brought to me, a white animal, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the Qur'an calls the donkey's voice the worst of voices, while explaining why the Buraq hesitated. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Go at a moderate pace and lower your voice, for the ugliest of all voices is the braying of asses.’

dalil.context: The Buraq is the vehicle of the prophets, and the ustaz says this hadith is hasan.
dalil.translation: Prophet Ibrahim AS used to come every month on the Buraq to visit his wife and son in Makkah.

dalil.context: The first verse of the seventeenth surah, which mentions the night journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa.
dalil.translation: Glory to Him who made His servant travel by night from the sacred place of worship to the furthest place of worship, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs: He alone is the All Hearing, the All Seeing.

dalil.context: The ustaz reminds us nothing is like Allah, so our imaginings do not reflect the reality. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: the Creator of the heavens and earth.’ He made mates for you from among yourselves––and for the animals too––so that you may multiply. There is nothing like Him: He is the All Hearing, the All Seeing.

dalil.context: The ustaz notes scholars differ on whether this hadith is authentic.
dalil.translation: Jibril told the Prophet to dismount and pray, then asked whether he knew where he had prayed. Jibril answered: you prayed at Taibah, the place of your Hijrah.

dalil.context: Another version names Mount Sinai, and the ustaz says this hadith is graded hasan.
dalil.translation: The Prophet was told he had prayed beside the tree of Prophet Musa AS in Madyan.

dalil.context: The last stop before Bayt al-Maqdis.
dalil.translation: Jibril told the Prophet he had prayed at Bayt Lahm, where Isa son of Maryam was born.

dalil.context: The Prophet tied the Buraq to the ring where the prophets tied it, then led the prophets.
dalil.translation: The prophets were gathered to me. Musa appeared like a sturdy man of the Shanu'ah tribe, and Isa son of Maryam prayed beside me, of medium height with fair skin.

dalil.context: The ustaz notes some scholars criticise the narration of that number.
dalil.translation: All the prophets stood behind the Prophet and prayed in congregation, and one narration puts their number at 124,000.

dalil.context: On this journey the Prophet prayed in all three mosques in one night.
dalil.translation: Do not strive to travel to any mosque except three: Masjid al-Haram, Masjid al-Nabawi and Masjid al-Aqsa.

dalil.context: The ustaz explains scholars say Adam AS built both, and Ibrahim AS rebuilt them.
dalil.translation: Abu Dharr asked which mosque was built first, and the Prophet said Masjid al-Haram, then Masjid al-Aqsa, with forty years between them.

dalil.context: Another narration gives three drinks, and Safiur Rahman cites only the Bukhari and Muslim version.
dalil.translation: Two vessels were offered to the Prophet, milk and wine, and he chose milk. Jibril said: you made a good choice, had you chosen wine your ummah would have gone astray.

dalil.context: The same procedure repeats at every heaven.
dalil.translation: Each gate of heaven is guarded by an angel who asks who is coming, who is with him, and whether he has been sent for. When told yes, the gate is opened with a welcome.

dalil.context: Allah adorned the lowest heaven with stars, giving an idea of how vast the first heaven is. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them [missiles] for stoning devils for whom We have also prepared the torment of a blazing fire.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Adam AS being sixty cubits tall in another hadith, and says this hadith is strong and undisputed.
dalil.translation: The Prophet saw Adam AS with his offspring, on the right the people of Paradise smiling and on the left the people of Hell weeping.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to a documentary saying there are rivers in the sky.
dalil.translation: The two visible rivers that begin from heaven are the Nile and the Euphrates.

dalil.context: They are cousins because Prophet Zakariya's wife was the sister of Maryam AS.
dalil.translation: The Prophet was raised to the second heaven and met two cousins, Isa and Yahya, who welcomed him.

dalil.context: The Prophet met Prophet Yusuf in the third heaven, and Surah Yusuf was revealed while he was grieving.
dalil.translation: Prophet Yusuf AS was given half of the beauty of all creation.

dalil.context: Allah raised Prophet Idris AS to a high station, and the Prophet met him in the fourth heaven.
dalil.translation: We raised him to a high position.

dalil.context: Prophet Musa is the figure the Prophet met most on this journey and became the benchmark of patience.
dalil.translation: Musa wept because a young man sent after him would have more of his ummah enter Paradise than Musa's.

dalil.context: Prophet Ibrahim was leaning on the Bayt al-Ma'mur in the seventh heaven.
dalil.translation: Prophet Ibrahim AS conveyed his greetings to the Prophet's ummah and told them to plant more in Paradise: its soil is fertile and its plants are tasbih, tahlil, tahmid and takbir.

dalil.context: The Bayt al-Ma'mur is aligned with the Ka'bah on earth.
dalil.translation: Every day 70,000 angels circumambulate the Bayt al-Ma'mur and never return to it.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to the angels descending on Laylat al-Qadr.
dalil.translation: I heard a rustling in the heaven like a bell, from the wings of angels glorifying Allah, and there is not four fingers' space without an angel prostrating.

dalil.context: Prophet Ibrahim asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead so his heart would be at ease, as the Prophet was strengthened through this journey. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead,’ He said, ‘Do you not believe, then?’ ‘Yes,’ said Abraham, ‘but just to put my heart at rest.’ So God said, ‘Take four birds and train them to come back to you. Then place them on separate hilltops, call them back, and they will come flying to you: know that God is all powerful and wise.’

dalil.context: The prohibition on backbiting as eating the flesh of one's brother, and the Prophet later saw the culprits punished. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Believers, avoid making too many assumptions- some assumptions are sinful- and do not spy on one another or speak ill of people behind their backs: would any of you like to eat the flesh of your dead brother? No, you would hate it. So be mindful of God: God is ever relenting, most merciful.

dalil.context: It shows the Prophet's love for a stubborn ummah.
dalil.translation: The Prophet is pictured like one standing before a fire, holding back moths from flying into it, yet they break free.

books.context: The prize-winning sirah that lists six opinions on the date of the Isra' and Mi'raj and cites Ibn Qayyim on trial and faith.
Source of the hadiths on the opening of the chest, Adam, Isa and Yahya, Musa, the first mosque and the choice of milk.
Source of the hadith of the Prophet seeing Musa and Isa at Bayt al-Maqdis.
Source of the hadith of the stop at Bayt Lahm and the narration of 124,000 prophets.
Describes the Prophet's face and features, which match Prophet Ibrahim's description in the Mi'raj hadith.
A National Geographic documentary showing that there are rivers in the sky.
A commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari that discusses the narrations of the Isra' and Mi'raj.
Collects and compares the narrations of the Isra' and Mi'raj.

people.context: Cited in Ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum: when a servant is tested at the highest level and is content and patient, Allah shows him what he never saw and his faith rises.
Lists six opinions on the date of the Isra' and chooses the view that it came after the deaths of Khadijah RA and Abu Talib and before the Hijrah.
Her death was part of the Prophet's grief before the Isra' and Mi'raj, and she died before the five daily prayers were made obligatory.
The most important figure in Makkah who enabled the Prophet's da'wah, and whose death was deeply painful.
Gave the Prophet protection to re-enter Makkah after Ta'if.
About 10 to 12 years old and still in Makkah when Khadijah RA died.
In one version the Prophet was staying at her house when the Isra' began.
Accompanied the Prophet throughout, opened his chest, rebuked the Buraq and answered his questions at each heaven.
Narrated the hadith of the prayer stop at Taibah.
Gave birth to Isa at Bayt Lahm with Jibril's help, and was the sister of Prophet Zakariya's wife.
Would later open Bayt al-Maqdis, take its keys and help clear the site of Masjid al-Aqsa.
Asked the Prophet about the first mosque built on earth and the distance between the two mosques.
Welcomed the Prophet in the first heaven with his offspring on the right and left.
Met at Bayt al-Maqdis and in the second heaven together with Yahya, his cousin.
Cousin of Isa, son of Prophet Zakariya who prayed without despair.
Given half the beauty of creation, met by the Prophet in the third heaven.
Met in the fourth heaven, and said to be the first to write with a pen.
Welcomed and prayed for the Prophet in the fifth heaven.
Met in the sixth heaven, wept because the Prophet's ummah would be more numerous in Paradise, and became the benchmark of patience in the Prophet's life.
Father of the prophets whose prayer was answered by the Prophet; welcomed him in the seventh heaven and sent greetings and a message of dhikr to the ummah.
The Prophet likened Prophet Isa AS to the face of Urwah.

lessons.title: The highest trial is met with strengthened faith
lessons.body: When a servant is tested at the highest level and is content and patient, Allah shows him what he never saw until his faith rises.

lessons.title: Rejecting the Isra' means rejecting the Qur'an
lessons.body: The Isra' is mentioned in the Qur'an so denying it denies Allah's verse, while denying the Mi'raj calls for more care in passing judgment.

lessons.title: Understand it through three contexts
lessons.body: The event must be understood through the textual context, the Prophet's life and Bayt al-Maqdis, and the world context of Rome and Persia.

lessons.title: Not every narration can be arranged, so stay calm
lessons.body: The Companions told the parts they remembered, so the chronology is hard to arrange and we need not worry if confused.

lessons.title: The mind cannot reach the reality, so glorify Allah
lessons.body: Subhanallah declares Allah pure and also admits what the mind cannot reach, like the reality of the Buraq and the journey.

lessons.title: The journey was in body and soul
lessons.body: The event was experienced in body and soul, and its miracle is that it was not merely a spiritual experience.

lessons.title: Choose what is pure and clarifying
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ chose milk, which is clean, strengthening and refreshing, not wine, which clouds the mind.

lessons.title: Masjid al-Aqsa must not be removed from the ummah's memory
lessons.body: All the prophets gathered at al-Aqsa and the Prophet ﷺ prayed there, so it is a place of great importance in faith and memory.

lessons.title: The uniformity of the prophets' message
lessons.body: All the prophets brought the same message and prayed with the same bowing and prostration, united behind the Prophet.

lessons.title: There is always a way, Allah is in control
lessons.body: When all seems closed, Allah shows that He holds every affair and never abandons His servant.

lessons.title: The Prophet's mercy grew after seeing the punishment
lessons.body: Having seen the fate of the disobedient, the Prophet ﷺ returned to a people who hurt him with more love and more effort.

lessons.title: Plant your garden in Paradise with dhikr
lessons.body: Prophet Ibrahim told the ummah to plant more in Paradise through tasbih, tahlil, tahmid and takbir.

lessons.title: Learn from Prophet Musa's patience
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ often recalled Prophet Musa, tested more heavily yet patient, making him the benchmark of patience.

lessons.title: Prayer is our mi'raj
lessons.body: We do not wait for the Buraq, but we can ascend in prayer, the worship for which Allah took the Prophet up to the heavens.

lessons.title: The biggest crisis is a severed bond with Allah
lessons.body: A prayer on autopilot or delayed shows the greatest crisis, greater than hardship in life.

glossary.meaning: The Prophet's night journey on earth from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa.
The Prophet's ascent from the earth through the heavens to the presence of Allah.
The area in Palestine containing Masjid al-Aqsa, where the prophets gathered in the Isra'.
The semicircular area beside the Ka'bah, also called al-Hatim, where the Prophet rested before the Isra'.
An accepted hadith, ranking below sahih.
The swift white mount of the prophets, from 'barq', meaning lightning.
A name of Madinah, where the Prophet prayed at the first stop.
The lote tree above the seventh heaven which the Prophet passed before meeting Allah.
The house in the seventh heaven aligned with the Ka'bah, where 70,000 angels circle daily.
